title: Quantum Gates Built on a Spin Qubit and a Kitaev Parity Qubit
authors: Zhi-Hai Liu, Jiang Zhang, Guilu Long, H. Q. Xu
abstract: Spin is typically traced out in the description of quantum-dot-based Kitaev chains to simplify the construction of Majorana fermions. Yet the intrinsic spin structure of poor-man's Majorana modes in minimal Kitaev chains under finite Zeeman fields offers a natural interface for the Kitaev parity qubit to interact with other spinful systems. Here, we establish such a platform to bridge the parity qubit and a quantum-dot spin qubit, with the effective coupling governed by the spin-dependent delocalization of the Majorana modes. Depending on whether the spin qubit is coupled to one or two chains constituting the parity qubit, the parity-spin coupling exhibits distinct forms: an anisotropic parity-conserving exchange interaction or a nontrivial exchange tensor tunable via the interchain superconducting-phase bias. Leveraging fast spin-qubit manipulation, we further demonstrate universal parity-qubit control, high-fidelity qubit-state readout, and entangling operations between the parity and spin qubits. These results turn the spinful structure of poor-man's Majoranas from a finite-field imperfection into a resource for hybrid quantum control.
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum computing platform coupling a Kitaev parity qubit to a spin qubit using Majorana fermions in a quantum dot array. By exploiting the spin-dependent nature of the Majorana modes, the authors derive tunable coupling mechanisms that enable the realization of universal quantum gates, demonstrating a path toward robust solid-state topological quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a functional platform to couple a Kitaev parity qubit (PQ) with a quantum-dot spin qubit (SQ) by utilizing the intrinsic spin structure of poor-man's Majorana modes (PMMs).
main_result: The system successfully supports universal control over the PQ, high-fidelity state readout, and the implementation of entangling gates (iSWAP, CZ) between the two qubits.
method: The analysis involves deriving effective coupling Hamiltonians based on the spin-dependent delocalization of PMMs and synthesizing quantum gates via controlled time evolution in different coupling regimes.
model_or_system: The physical system is an SM-SC hybrid quantum dot array integrating the PQ (built on PMMs in Minimal Kitaev Chains) and the SQ (encoded in Zeeman-split QD states). The coupling is mediated by tunneling channels between the sites.
key_observables: Gate fidelities (e.g., CZ gate fidelity reaching 99%), coupling strengths (tens of MHz), and the spin-dependent delocalization coefficients.
important_parameters: Interchain superconducting-phase bias ($\Phi_0$), Zeeman splitting ($\Delta_z$), and the tunneling barrier strengths ($V_1, V_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the strong intradot Coulomb repulsion regime ($U$) and that the spinless description of MKCs is valid, which requires a large Zeeman splitting.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the QD array integrating PQ and SQ. Figure 2 illustrates the BdG spectrum and spin-dependent delocalization coefficients versus $\Delta_z$. Figure 4 provides a guide showing coupling configurations and quantum circuits for various gates.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and the role of PMM spin structure in coupling. It then analyzes the effective Hamiltonians across different coupling regimes (Type-(i), (ii), (iii)). Finally, it demonstrates the synthesis of single-qubit and two-qubit quantum gates using these derived Hamiltonians.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the challenge of integrating topological qubits (Majorana-based) with conventional solid-state qubits (spin qubits) for scalable quantum computation, which is a major focus in quantum information theory.

EF , Vc, and U denote the Fermi level and the confinement and Coulomb energies of Q0.
